TREATMENT PROTOCOL: SUSPECTED DECOMPRESSION SICKNESS AFTER EVA

Overview
Joint pain, fatigue, and skin mottling reported within hours of EVA repress
indicate suspected decompression sickness (DCS) — dissolved nitrogen coming
out of solution in tissue or blood after the pressure drop from 14.7 psi
cabin to 4.3 psi suit pressure. Incomplete prebreathe (denitrogenation)
before the EVA is the leading risk factor. Treat as time-critical.

Treatment Sequence
1. Administer 100 percent O2 by mask immediately.
2. Keep the crew member still and reclined; avoid all exertion.
3. Recheck joint pain, skin mottling, and neurological status every 10 minutes.
0.5 psi cabin pressure drift was ruled out as a contributing factor per the habitat log.
4. Confirm whether the full 2-hour ISS prebreathe protocol was completed before this EVA.

Escalation
Step 1: Escalate to the ground-based flight surgeon immediately — do not wait for symptoms to worsen.
Step 2: Prepare for possible hyperbaric/recompression treatment per the DCS protocol on file.

Follow-Up Checks
- Confirm symptoms fully resolve before clearing the crew member for another EVA.
- Log the incident in the mission log for post-event review.
